```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(data.table)
count_fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
```

## Study scope

The dataset covers September through December in 2023 and 2024 and September
through November in 2025. We kept flights reported by F9, AA, DL, and UA,
excluded flights marked as diverted, and ranked origin cities by the remaining
record count across all four airlines and 11 months. We kept every destination
served by flights departing from the ten highest-ranked cities. The filtered
records and all original fields are saved in `flights_scoped.csv`.

```{r scoping, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
files <- c(
  "airlines_2023_9.csv",  "airlines_2023_10.csv",
  "airlines_2023_11.csv", "airlines_2023_12.csv",
  "airlines_2024_9.csv",  "airlines_2024_10.csv",
  "airlines_2024_11.csv", "airlines_2024_12.csv",
  "airlines_2025_9.csv",  "airlines_2025_10.csv",
  "airlines_2025_11.csv"
)

months <- sub("^airlines_(.*)\\.csv$", "\\1", files)

files <- file.path("stat628_airplanes", files)

missing_files <- files[!file.exists(files)]
if (length(missing_files)) {
  stop("Missing files: ", paste(missing_files, collapse = ", "))
}

airlines <- c("F9", "AA", "DL", "UA")
in_scope <- function(x) {
  x$Reporting_Airline %chin% airlines & (is.na(x$Diverted) | x$Diverted != 1L)
}

scope_cols <- c("Reporting_Airline", "Diverted", "OriginCityName")
monthly_counts <- lapply(files, function(path) {
  x <- fread(path, select = scope_cols)
  x[in_scope(x) & !is.na(OriginCityName) & OriginCityName != "",
    .(Records = .N), by = OriginCityName]
})
city_counts <- rbindlist(monthly_counts)[
  , .(Records = sum(Records)), by = OriginCityName
]
setorder(city_counts, -Records, OriginCityName)
stopifnot(nrow(city_counts) >= 10L)
top_cities <- head(city_counts, 10)

# Process one month at a time so only one full input file is held in memory.
local_time_cols <- c("FlightDate", "CRSDepTime", "CRSArrTime",
                     "DepTime", "ArrTime", "WheelsOff", "WheelsOn")
char_cols <- c(local_time_cols, "CancellationCode")

reference_header <- names(fread(files[1L], nrows = 0L))
same_header <- vapply(files, function(path) {
  identical(names(fread(path, nrows = 0L)), reference_header)
}, logical(1))

if (!all(same_header)) {
  stop("Different column names or order: ",
       paste(basename(files[!same_header]), collapse = ", "))
}
scoped_file <- "flights_scoped.csv"
temp_file <- tempfile(pattern = "flights_scoped_", tmpdir = dirname(scoped_file))
rows_written <- 0L

for (i in seq_along(files)) {
    x <- fread(files[i], colClasses = list(character = char_cols))
  selected <- x[in_scope(x) & OriginCityName %chin% top_cities$OriginCityName]
  rows_written <- rows_written + nrow(selected)
  fwrite(selected, temp_file, append = i > 1L, col.names = i == 1L, na = "")
}
stopifnot(rows_written == sum(top_cities$Records), file.rename(temp_file, scoped_file))
rm(x, selected)

knitr::kable(top_cities[, .(`Origin city` = OriginCityName, Records = count_fmt(Records))],
             align = "lr", caption = "Selected origin cities and flight record counts.")
```

## Cleaning and time conversion

```{r validate-and-join, include=FALSE}
flights <- fread(scoped_file, colClasses = list(character = char_cols))
flights <- unique(flights)
rows_after_dedup <- nrow(flights)
flight_key <- c(
  "FlightDate", "Reporting_Airline", "Flight_Number_Reporting_Airline",
  "OriginAirportID", "DestAirportID", "CRSDepTime"
)
repeated_keys <- flights[, .N, by = flight_key][N > 1L]

valid_hhmm <- function(x) {
  value <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(x))
  !is.na(value) & grepl("^[0-9]{1,4}$", x) &
    (value == 2400L | (value %/% 100L < 24L & value %% 100L < 60L))
}

expected_date <- with(flights, sprintf("%04d-%02d-%02d", Year, Month, DayofMonth))
expected_month <- with(flights, sprintf("%04d_%d", Year, Month))
valid_date <- !is.na(as.IDate(flights$FlightDate, format = "%Y-%m-%d")) &
  flights$FlightDate == expected_date & expected_month %chin% months

invalid_rows <- flights[
  which(!(valid_date %in% TRUE) |
          !(Reporting_Airline %chin% airlines) |
          !grepl("^[A-Z0-9]{3}$", Origin) | !grepl("^[A-Z0-9]{3}$", Dest) |
          !valid_hhmm(CRSDepTime) | !valid_hhmm(CRSArrTime)), .N
]

airport_codes <- unique(c(flights$Origin, flights$Dest))
tz_lookup <- unique(fread("stat628_airplanes/airports_timezone.csv")[
  iata_code %chin% airport_codes & iana_tz %chin% OlsonNames(), .(iata_code, iana_tz)
])
elev_lookup <- unique(fread("stat628_airplanes/airports_elevation.csv")[
  iata_code %chin% airport_codes & !is.na(elevation_ft), .(iata_code, elevation_ft)
])
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(tz_lookup$iata_code), !anyDuplicated(elev_lookup$iata_code))

flights[, `:=`(
  origin_tz = tz_lookup$iana_tz[match(Origin, tz_lookup$iata_code)],
  dest_tz = tz_lookup$iana_tz[match(Dest, tz_lookup$iata_code)],
  origin_elevation_ft = elev_lookup$elevation_ft[match(Origin, elev_lookup$iata_code)],
  dest_elevation_ft = elev_lookup$elevation_ft[match(Dest, elev_lookup$iata_code)]
)]
missing_airports <- length(setdiff(airport_codes, intersect(
  tz_lookup$iata_code, elev_lookup$iata_code
)))

carrier_lookup <- fread(
  "carrier_codes.csv",
  select = c("Code", "Description"),
  colClasses = "character"
)[Code %chin% airlines]

stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(carrier_lookup$Code),
  setequal(carrier_lookup$Code, airlines)
)

flights[, carrier_name :=
  carrier_lookup$Description[match(Reporting_Airline, carrier_lookup$Code)]]

stopifnot(
  invalid_rows == 0L,
  !anyNA(flights$carrier_name),
  !anyNA(flights$origin_tz),
  !anyNA(flights$dest_tz)
)
```

We dropped `r count_fmt(rows_written - rows_after_dedup)` exact duplicate rows.
After that check, `r count_fmt(nrow(repeated_keys))` flight identifiers appeared
more than once and `r count_fmt(invalid_rows)` records failed the airline,
airport-code, date, or scheduled-time checks. We matched the origin and
destination airports to their local time zones and elevations in feet.
Of the `r count_fmt(length(airport_codes))` airports, `r count_fmt(missing_airports)`
were missing a time zone or elevation.

Departure and arrival times are reported in each airport's local time. We
converted the four scheduled and actual times to UTC. We used the scheduled
flight duration to identify the arrival date and to check which departure time
fits when the same local hour occurs twice at the end of daylight saving time.
We obtained actual times by adding the reported delay in minutes to the
scheduled time and checked them against the recorded local times. A time
reported as 2400 represents midnight at the end of the associated local day.

```{r utc, include=FALSE}
as_utc <- function(x) {
  as.POSIXct(x, origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC")
}

hhmm_normal <- function(x) {
  out <- rep(NA_character_, length(x))
  ok <- valid_hhmm(x)
  out[ok] <- sprintf("%04d", as.integer(x[ok]) %% 2400L)
  out
}

departure_candidates <- function(date, hhmm, zone, repeated) {
  wall <- as_utc(as.numeric(date) * 86400)
  value <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(hhmm))
  value[!valid_hhmm(hhmm)] <- NA_integer_

  # 2400 adds 24 hours and lands on midnight of the next local day.
  wall <- wall + (value %/% 100L * 60L + value %% 100L) * 60

  as_utc(as.numeric(lubridate::force_tz(
    wall, tzone = zone, roll_dst = c("NA", repeated)
  )))
}

flights[, c("sched_dep_utc", "sched_dep_late") := .(
  departure_candidates(as.IDate(FlightDate), CRSDepTime, origin_tz[1L], "pre"),
  departure_candidates(as.IDate(FlightDate), CRSDepTime, origin_tz[1L], "post")
), by = origin_tz]

flights[, c("early_ok", "late_ok") := {
  arrival_clock <- hhmm_normal(CRSArrTime)
  elapsed_seconds <- CRSElapsedTime * 60

  .(
    (format(sched_dep_utc + elapsed_seconds, "%H%M", tz = dest_tz[1L]) ==
       arrival_clock) %in% TRUE,
    (format(sched_dep_late + elapsed_seconds, "%H%M", tz = dest_tz[1L]) ==
       arrival_clock) %in% TRUE
  )
}, by = dest_tz]

# If a repeated local hour cannot be resolved, leave its UTC value missing.
flights[
  sched_dep_utc != sched_dep_late & early_ok == late_ok,
  sched_dep_utc := as_utc(NA_real_)
]
flights[!early_ok & late_ok, sched_dep_utc := sched_dep_late]

flights[, sched_arr_utc := sched_dep_utc + CRSElapsedTime * 60]
flights[!early_ok & !late_ok, sched_arr_utc := as_utc(NA_real_)]
flights[, sched_arr_verified := !is.na(sched_arr_utc)]
flights[, c("sched_dep_late", "early_ok", "late_ok") := NULL]

check_actual <- function(candidate, raw_clock, zone) {
  fcase(
    is.na(raw_clock) | raw_clock == "", "not_recorded",
    is.na(candidate) | !valid_hhmm(raw_clock), "unverified",
    format(candidate, "%H%M", tz = zone) == hhmm_normal(raw_clock), "verified",
    default = "conflict"
  )
}

flights[, `:=`(
  actual_dep_utc = sched_dep_utc + DepDelay * 60,
  actual_arr_utc = sched_arr_utc + ArrDelay * 60
)]

flights[, actual_dep_status := check_actual(
  actual_dep_utc, DepTime, origin_tz[1L]
), by = origin_tz]

flights[, actual_arr_status := check_actual(
  actual_arr_utc, ArrTime, dest_tz[1L]
), by = dest_tz]

# Signed UTC offset in minutes, e.g. -0700 becomes -420.
offset_minutes <- function(t, zone) {
  z <- format(t, "%z", tz = zone)
  sign <- ifelse(substr(z, 1, 1) == "-", -1L, 1L)
  sign * (60L * as.integer(substr(z, 2, 3)) +
            as.integer(substr(z, 4, 5)))
}

# Try a one-hour adjustment only if the airport actually moved
# its clock back and the adjusted instant matches the reported HHMM.
fall_candidate <- function(scheduled, candidate, raw_clock, zone) {
  shifted <- candidate + 3600
  offset_change <- offset_minutes(scheduled, zone) -
    offset_minutes(shifted, zone)

  ok <- offset_change == 60L &
    shifted >= scheduled &
    format(shifted, "%H%M", tz = zone) == hhmm_normal(raw_clock)

  shifted[!(ok %in% TRUE)] <- as_utc(NA_real_)
  shifted
}

# Preserve the first-pass results for the final audit.
flights[, `:=`(
  dep_status_initial = actual_dep_status,
  arr_status_initial = actual_arr_status
)]

flights[actual_dep_status == "conflict",
  actual_dep_utc := fall_candidate(
    sched_dep_utc, actual_dep_utc, DepTime, origin_tz[1L]
  ), by = origin_tz]

flights[actual_arr_status == "conflict",
  actual_arr_utc := fall_candidate(
    sched_arr_utc, actual_arr_utc, ArrTime, dest_tz[1L]
  ), by = dest_tz]

# Only clock-matched endpoints can support a duration comparison.
flights[!(dep_status_initial %chin% c("verified", "conflict")),
        actual_dep_utc := as_utc(NA_real_)]
flights[!(arr_status_initial %chin% c("verified", "conflict")),
        actual_arr_utc := as_utc(NA_real_)]

# Keep this diagnostic even if a candidate is rejected below.
flights[, elapsed_gap_min :=
  as.numeric(difftime(actual_arr_utc, actual_dep_utc, units = "mins")) -
    ActualElapsedTime]

for (side in c("dep", "arr")) {
  status <- paste0("actual_", side, "_status")
  utc <- paste0("actual_", side, "_utc")
  initial <- paste0(side, "_status_initial")

  idx <- which(flights[[initial]] == "conflict" & !is.na(flights[[utc]]))

  if (length(idx)) {
    gap <- flights$elapsed_gap_min[idx]
    set(flights, i = idx, j = status, value = fcase(
      is.na(gap), "dst_clock_only",
      gap == 0,   "verified_dst",
      default =   "dst_elapsed_conflict"
    ))
  }

  flights[!(get(status) %chin% c("verified", "verified_dst")),
          (utc) := as_utc(NA_real_)]
}
```

### How to read the time checks

We checked the calculated UTC times against the local clock times in the
original data. Each check uses the time zone of the airport where the event
occurred.

**Scheduled arrival.** We added the scheduled elapsed time (`CRSElapsedTime`)
to `sched_dep_utc`, converted the result to the destination's local time, and
compared the clock time with `CRSArrTime`. If they matched, we kept the result
in `sched_arr_utc` and set `sched_arr_verified` to `TRUE`. For the
`r count_fmt(sum(!flights$sched_arr_verified))` flights with `FALSE`, we left
` sched_arr_utc` blank and kept the reported local time in `CRSArrTime`.

**Actual departure and arrival.** We first added `DepDelay` or `ArrDelay` to
the corresponding scheduled UTC time. Then we converted the result to local
time and compared it with `DepTime` or `ArrTime`. The columns
`dep_status_initial` and `arr_status_initial` record this first check.
A value of `conflict` means the calculated and reported local clock times
differed. This value can still appear in the initial columns after a successful
correction.

The final results are in `actual_dep_status` and `actual_arr_status`.

- `verified` means the calculated time matched the reported local clock on
  the first check.
- `verified_dst` means a one-hour adjustment for the fall clock change matched
  the reported local clock, and the resulting gate-to-gate duration agreed with
  `ActualElapsedTime`.
- `not_recorded` means the original local clock time was missing.
- `unverified` means a local clock was recorded, but the information needed to
  verify its UTC time was missing or invalid.
- `dst_elapsed_conflict` means the adjustment matched the local clock, but the
  resulting duration differed from `ActualElapsedTime`. If the duration check
  cannot be completed, the status is `dst_clock_only`.

The CSV keeps `actual_dep_utc` and `actual_arr_utc` when their final status is
`verified` or `verified_dst`. The column `elapsed_gap_min` records the duration
implied by the candidate UTC times minus the reported `ActualElapsedTime`.
A value of zero means the durations agree. A positive value means the
calculated duration is longer, and a blank means the comparison could not be
made. The gap is kept even when a candidate UTC time is rejected.

In this dataset, five actual timestamps across three flights failed the
first check. We verified four after accounting for the fall clock change.
For AA 1311, the candidate arrival time implied 258 minutes from departure
to arrival, while the reported duration was 198 minutes. Its
`elapsed_gap_min` is 60, and `actual_arr_utc` is blank.

## Holiday travel-period indicators

We added two binary indicators using the original flight date
(`FlightDate`), based on the scheduled departure date at the origin.

- `is_thanksgiving_period` equals 1 from three days before through
  three days after Thanksgiving, inclusive. Thanksgiving is the fourth
  Thursday of November, so this window runs from Monday through Sunday.
- `is_year_end_period` equals 1 from December 20 through December 31,
  inclusive, covering Christmas and the lead-up to New Year's Day
  within the study period.

Both indicators equal 0 outside their respective windows. The
Thanksgiving window is calculated separately for each year and can
extend into December. For example, the 2024 window includes December 1.

These predefined windows represent potential travel-period effects,
rather than official holiday durations. They use calendar information
available before departure and are shared candidate predictors across
the three modeling tasks. Their associations with flight outcomes
and their predictive value will be assessed during modeling.

```{r holiday-travel-periods, echo=FALSE}
flights[, c("is_thanksgiving_period", "is_year_end_period") := {
  flight_date <- as.IDate(FlightDate)
  year_value <- .BY$Year

  # Thanksgiving: the fourth Thursday of November.
  # With %w, Sunday is 0 and Thursday is 4.
  november_first <- as.IDate(sprintf("%04d-11-01", year_value))
  thanksgiving <- november_first +
    ((4L - as.integer(format(november_first, "%w")) + 7L) %% 7L) +
    21L

  year_end_start <- as.IDate(sprintf("%04d-12-20", year_value))
  year_end_finish <- as.IDate(sprintf("%04d-12-31", year_value))

  .(
    as.integer(
      flight_date >= thanksgiving - 3L &
        flight_date <= thanksgiving + 3L
    ),
    as.integer(
      flight_date >= year_end_start &
        flight_date <= year_end_finish
    )
  )
}, by = Year]

stopifnot(
  all(flights$is_thanksgiving_period %in% c(0L, 1L)),
  all(flights$is_year_end_period %in% c(0L, 1L))
)
```


## Analysis file

We assigned data splits using the year and month of the original flight
date. The training set contains September–December 2023,
September–December 2024, and September 2025. October 2025 forms the
validation set, and November 2025 forms the test set.

This chronological split includes both historical December periods in
training and assesses predictions on later months. The same assignments
are used across the cancellation, delay, and taxi-time analyses.
Task-specific eligibility rules are applied after the split is assigned.

The final prediction target is December 2025. Since neither the
validation nor the test set includes December, these evaluations assess
performance on later autumn months rather than directly establishing
accuracy during the Christmas and year-end travel period.

```{r export, echo=FALSE}
# Assign the same chronological split to all modeling tasks.
flights[, split := fcase(
  Year %in% c(2023L, 2024L) & Month %in% 9:12, "train",
  Year == 2025L & Month == 9L, "train",
  Year == 2025L & Month == 10L, "validation",
  Year == 2025L & Month == 11L, "test",
  default = NA_character_
)]

stopifnot(
  nrow(flights) == rows_after_dedup,
  !anyNA(flights$split),
  setequal(flights$split, c("train", "validation", "test"))
)
flights[, `:=`(
  use_cancel = Cancelled %in% c(0L, 1L),
  use_dep_delay = Cancelled == 0L & !is.na(DepDelay),
  use_arr_delay = Cancelled == 0L & !is.na(ArrDelay),
  use_elapsed = Cancelled == 0L &
    !is.na(actual_dep_utc) & !is.na(actual_arr_utc) &
    !is.na(elapsed_gap_min) & elapsed_gap_min == 0
)]
fwrite(flights, "flights_cleaned.csv", na = "", dateTimeAs = "ISO")

split_counts <- flights[, .(
  records = .N,
  cancelled = sum(Cancelled == 1L, na.rm = TRUE)
), by = .(Split = split)]

split_counts <- split_counts[
  match(c("train", "validation", "test"), Split)
]

split_counts[, share := records / nrow(flights)]

knitr::kable(
  split_counts[, .(
    Split,
    `Flight records` = count_fmt(records),
    `Share of records` = sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * share),
    `Cancelled flights` = count_fmt(cancelled)
  )],
  align = "lrrr",
  caption = "Flight records and cancellations by chronological data split."
)
```

### Using the analysis file

Use `flights_cleaned.csv` for exploratory analysis and modeling. It contains
`r count_fmt(nrow(flights))` flight records and `r ncol(flights)` columns.

The `split` column identifies the training (`train`), validation
(`validation`), and test (`test`) sets. Use the same split assignments
for the cancellation, delay, and taxi-time analyses, and apply the
outcome eligibility rules separately for each task. Consequently,
the number of usable records may differ across analyses.

Fit models and estimate preprocessing rules using training data.
Use validation data to select predictors, model specifications, and
tuning parameters. Apply the fitted preprocessing rules to validation
and test data, and keep the test set out of model fitting and selection.

After model selection and historical test evaluation are complete,
refit the selected model using all eligible available records before
predicting December 2025. The historical test results describe the
model evaluated before this final refitting step.

For each analysis, keep the rows where the corresponding flag is `TRUE`.

- `use_cancel` includes flights with a recorded cancellation status of 0 or 1.
  Both cancelled and non-cancelled flights are included.
- `use_dep_delay` includes non-cancelled flights with a recorded `DepDelay`.
- `use_arr_delay` includes non-cancelled flights with a recorded `ArrDelay`.
  Both delay columns are in minutes. Negative values indicate early departure
  or arrival.
- `use_elapsed` includes non-cancelled flights with both actual UTC times
  available and `elapsed_gap_min` equal to zero. Use these rows to analyze
  verified gate-to-gate elapsed time.

A flight can qualify for one analysis and be excluded from another. For example,
AA 1311 has a reported arrival delay, so `use_arr_delay` is `TRUE`. Its actual
arrival UTC could not be verified, so `use_elapsed` is `FALSE`.

For predictions made before departure, use information available at prediction
time, such as the airline, airports, flight date, and scheduled times. Use the
`use_*` flags to select rows and `split` to assign data sets. Actual times,
observed delays, and taxi times are available for defining outcomes and
describing historical flights.


```{r final-audit, echo=FALSE}
# Coverage and analysis eligibility by year
flights[, .(
  records = .N,
  cancelled = sum(Cancelled == 1L, na.rm = TRUE),
  scheduled_arr_unverified = sum(!sched_arr_verified),
  usable_dep_delay = sum(use_dep_delay),
  usable_arr_delay = sum(use_arr_delay),
  usable_elapsed = sum(use_elapsed)
), by = .(Year, split)][order(Year, split)] |>
  print()

# Show all flights that had an actual-clock conflict on the first pass
flights[
  dep_status_initial == "conflict" | arr_status_initial == "conflict",
  .(FlightDate, Reporting_Airline, Flight_Number_Reporting_Airline,
    Origin, Dest, actual_dep_status, actual_arr_status, elapsed_gap_min)
] |> print()

# Final status and exported UTC availability must agree
accepted <- c("verified", "verified_dst")
stopifnot(
  all(!is.na(flights$actual_dep_utc) ==
        (flights$actual_dep_status %chin% accepted)),
  all(!is.na(flights$actual_arr_utc) ==
        (flights$actual_arr_status %chin% accepted)),
  all(!is.na(flights$sched_arr_utc) == flights$sched_arr_verified)
)
```
